Arsonist Starts Fire At Golders Green Apartment Building
content:
An arsonist started a fire in a stairwell of a Golders Green apartment building where most of the residents are Jewish, and many are young families, the Shomrim organization in London reported.
The incident began when a fire alarm went off in the early hours of Tuesday morning. Residents reported that they witnessed a suspect deliberately setting a fire in the stairwell. He fled the scene when confronted by residents.
One of the residents acted quickly to extinguish the fire, preventing what could have turned into a far more serious incident. B’Chasdei Hashem, no injuries were reported.
Shomrim volunteers collected evidence believed to belong to the arsonist and transferred it to the police.
The disturbing incident comes less than a month after two Jews were seriously injured in a stabbing incident in Golders Green and two months after four Hatzolah ambulances were set on fire in Golders Green.
(YWN Israel Desk—Jerusalem)

title: Explosion and fire at a Dallas apartment building kills at least 3 people , including a child
content:
Explosion and fire at a Dallas apartment building kills at least 3 people, including a child
DALLAS (AP) — An explosion and massive fire at a Dallas apartment building Thursday killed a child and at least two other people following a blast that shook nearby homes and happened while firefighters were rushing to a reported gas leak, officials said.
At least five people also went to hospitals with injuries, Dallas Fire-Rescue spokesperson Jason Evans said. It was unclear how many residents lived in the two-story complex in the Oak Cliff neighborhood south of downtown Dallas, where a towering plume of black smoke was visible for miles.
Evans did not rule out that more victims could be found as crews continued to sift through the charred remains of the building. By late Thursday, Evans said firefighters had searched less than half of the scene by hand and that some areas would require excavation.
“This was enormous,” Evans said of the fire.
As dozens of firefighters swarmed to the neighborhood, some residents’ friends and relatives worried as they tried unsuccessfully to reach each loved ones. Dozens of firefighters searched through the smoldering rubble of the building even as colleagues continued to drench the blackened debris.
Berry said firefighters were responding to a call of a gas leak when an explosion happened.
“We had the cavalry coming,” Dallas Fire-Rescue Deputy Chief Mark Berry said. ”But the explosion had already taken place.”
Atmos Energy, a natural gas provider, said in a statement they were told by fire officials that a construction crew unrelated to the company had damaged a pipeline near the site of the fire.
Kacee Proctor, a resident of the apartment building, said her mother had smelled gas inside a day earlier, but Proctor didn’t think much of it at the time.
She wasn’t home during the blast and was devastated that her cat, Shirley, was stuck inside.
“I’ve been sitting over there crying for several hours. I don’t know what to do. This is all I have right here,” Proctor said, gesturing to the clothes she was wearing.
She spent the afternoon chatting with neighbors who had evacuated, including a girl who was home babysitting her little sister and carried both the child and their dog to safety.
Natural gas service to the area remained shut off, and company officials were working with investigators on-site, the company said.
Authorities set up a family reunification center at a nearby high school. Several hours after the blaze, Frances Rizo was still trying to find her friend who lived in the building.
“She’s not answering her phone,” Rizo said.
Firefighters rushed to the scene as flames and black smoke billowed into the sky. Some trained their hoses on piles of smoking debris while others removed lumber and other burned wreckage to look for anyone trapped underneath. Little more than a blackened shell of the original building remained.
“The fire is contained, but our members are still working on the scene to do primary searches,” said Dallas Fire-Rescue Assistant Chief James Russ.
Julie Jensen said she was at home less than a block from the burning building when she heard a noise like an explosion that left her ears ringing.
“I was sitting on my couch watching TV — stuff flew off our walls,” Jensen said.
Jensen said she saw rising smoke and neighbors running when she looked out the window. She grabbed her family’s cat and left, finding a nearby parking lot to wait until she knew it was safe to return.
Sal De La Rosa was at work at a nearby auto repair shop when “all of a sudden we just heard and felt this huge boom.”
“We felt where the building kind of shook a little bit,” De La Rosa said.
He said a co-worker went outside and saw thick, black smoke rising into the air.
___
This story has been updated to correct the spelling of Frances Rizo’s last name in one instance. It is Rizo, not Rizzo.
___
Associated Press journalists Jim Vertuno in Austin, Texas, Russ Bynum in Savannah, Georgia, and Hannah Schoenbaum in Salt Lake City contributed.

Skokie apartment fire: Elderly woman seriously injured, witness describes chaos
SKOKIE, Ill. - A late-night fire at a Skokie apartment building sent an 84-year-old woman to the hospital and reportedly left residents scrambling to get out.
What we know:
Firefighters and police responded around 10:08 p.m. Monday to a multifamily building in the 9500 block of Bronx Place and found heavy smoke on the third floor, according to the Skokie Fire Department.
Crews contained the fire to a single unit within about 20 minutes.
Officials said one resident, an 84-year-old woman, was seriously injured and taken to an area hospital.
What they're saying:
A resident described the chaotic moment as neighbors rushed to warn one another.
"I started hearing like people running within the hallways of my building, people knocking, banging on doors, screaming," she said.
What we don't know:
The cause of the fire is still unknown, and no damage estimate was immediately available.
What's next:
The unit where the fire broke out was deemed uninhabitable, but all other residents were allowed back into their homes once crews completed their work.
The Source: The information in this story came from the Skokie Fire Department and a witness interview.

content:
More than 20 firefighters, supported by six vehicles—including a specialized aerial platform—responded to a major fire that broke out in an apartment on the first floor of a residential building in Drapetsona, a suburb of Piraeus in Attica. The blaze erupted around 5:15 a.m. on Thursday, May 21, 2026, at the intersection of Papastratou and Sparta streets.
Smoke Overwhelms Entire Building
Firefighters rushed to the scene and immediately began evacuating residents from the building. According to ERT News, the fire is burning uncontrolled, and thick, toxic smoke has filled not only the affected unit but also spread throughout the rest of the apartment complex, severely compromising air quality and visibility in neighboring apartments.
Elderly Resident Refuses Evacuation
An elderly woman residing on the third floor has refused to leave her home despite repeated efforts by firefighters and police officers. Emergency responders have administered oxygen due to smoke inhalation and continue working to safely evacuate her.
Preliminary Cause: LPG Cylinder
Initial reports suggest the fire originated from a liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) cylinder. The apartment’s occupants—a mother and her son—evacuated immediately after the fire started and are reported to be safe.

content:
South County firefighters rescue 2 people, dog from third-floor apartment fire
SNOHOMISH COUNTY, Wash. — Two adults and a dog were rescued from a third-floor apartment window after a fire tore through a Mountlake Terrace apartment building early Sunday, displacing more than a dozen households.
Firefighters responded to the Taluswood Apartments in the 4300 block of 236th St. SW shortly after 12 a.m. and found heavy smoke and fire coming from a three-story building. Crews spotted two adults at a window of an upper-floor unit and used a ladder to rescue both people and a dog.
The man and woman, both approximately in their 20s, were taken to Swedish Edmonds Hospital in stable condition and have since been discharged. The dog did not require medical intervention.
Fire spread across the second and third floors and into the attic of the impacted building. Firefighters searched 12 primarily affected units and evacuated residents from 12 adjacent units. Everyone else escaped safely, officials said.
After the fire was controlled, crews continued extinguishing hotspots until about 2 a.m. One firefighter was treated at the scene for a minor injury. Two additional civilians were evaluated by firefighters and did not require further medical care.
Residents in 13 apartment units were displaced, including at least 24 adults, one child, and 15 pets. Support 7 and American Red Cross volunteers are assisting those residents with immediate needs.
The Snohomish County Fire Marshal’s Office is investigating the cause of the fire. Damage estimates were not yet available. Shoreline Fire and Bothell Fire Department assisted in the response.
Fire officials also urged residents to have a home fire escape plan and working smoke alarms, noting that modern homes can burn faster due to synthetic furniture and open layouts. Smoke alarms should be replaced every 10 years and installed in every bedroom, outside every sleeping area, and on every level of a home.

Firefighters save dozens from midnight apartment fire in Mountlake Terrace, WA
EVERETT, Wash. - A late night fire north of Seattle caused a large response from area firefighters as they worked to rescue people and pets from the apartment building. In total, 24 adults, one child and 15 pets have been displaced by the fire.
Timeline:
Just after midnight heading into Sunday morning, South County firefighters were dispatched to a three-story apartment building in Mountlake Terrace on 236th Street SW.
Two people were reportedly spotted asking for help from a third floor window. Firefighters were able to get a ladder up to them and a dog to rescue them. Meanwhile, additional firefighters were called in to assist with the growing fire.
The 2-alarm fire caused residents from 12 apartments to be evacuated. Firefighting personnel spent more than two hours putting the fire out and addressing hot spots on the structure to prevent ignition.

A man and woman, both in their 20s were transported to Swedish hospital in Edmonds and discharged. The dog did not require medical attention, according to South County Fire.

Dog killed after fire fills Cincinnati apartment building with smoke
CINCINNATI (WKRC) - A dog died after a fire filled a west side Cincinnati apartment building with smoke Tuesday morning, according to fire officials.
Crews with Green Township Fire & EMS responded around 9:18 a.m. to the 6700 block of Harrison Avenue after receiving reports of smoke throughout the apartment complex.
Firefighters arrived to find a working fire inside a second-floor apartment and quickly launched an interior attack. Officials said the fire was brought under control by 9:33 a.m.
One dog died from smoke exposure, but no residents or firefighters were injured.
Multiple fire departments responded to assist, including crews from Miami Township, Cheviot, Whitewater Township and Colerain Township.
The cause of the apartment fire remains under investigation, though officials said it is not considered suspicious.

title: Residents displaced , one treated for smoke inhalation after apartment complex fire
content:
Residents displaced, one treated for smoke inhalation after apartment complex fire
SAN ANTONIO - A large fire at a two-story apartment building early Saturday morning has displaced multiple residents and caused extensive damage to the complex.
The fire started around 7:30 a.m., with fire crews arriving to find heavy flames spreading across both the first and second floors of the building. Due to the intensity of the fire, additional resources were requested, and crews were forced to shift to a defensive strategy, battling the fire from outside.
At least half of the building is expected to be a total loss. All residents of the affected building have been displaced as a result of the fire.
One person was evaluated and treated at the scene for minor smoke inhalation.
Apartment management is on-site working to help residents find temporary housing, and the Red Cross is on standby to provide additional assistance if needed.

title: Two rescued from Kansas apartment fire , 3 pets died
content:
RILEY COUNTY—Two people were rescued and hospitalized after an apartment fire in Manhattan.
At 6:13 a.m. on Tuesday, the Manhattan Fire Department was dispatched to an apartment building fire at 509 Pierre Street in Manhattan, according to a media release. Upon arrival, crews found a two-story residential building with smoke and flames showing from the second floor, and two persons on the porch roof.
A passerby had put up a ladder, climbed onto the porch roof, and helped an occupant out of a second-floor window and onto the porch roof.
The driver of firetruck Quint 2 raised a fire department ladder, allowing the two to come down. Firefighters then entered the building to search for another occupant reported to be trapped inside.
Firefighters found the person unconscious on the second floor and quickly removed them from the building. Both occupants of the second-floor apartment were transported by Riley County EMS.
There were four occupants of the building in total, with two escaping the first-floor apartment fire prior to the fire department's arrival. The passerby was uninjured. One dog was transported by Riley County Animal Control to Kansas State Vet Med. Two dogs and a cat perished in the fire.
The cause of the fire is under investigation at this time. The Kansas State Fire Marshal's Office and Riley County Police Department are assisting Manhattan Fire Investigators with the investigation.

content:
Chimney fire at Tower Point Condominiums prompts swift evacuation; no injuries reported
John Garcia arrived at the Tower Point Condominiums to see what was happening after smelling smoke from a friend’s house.
When he got there, he saw flames coming from a 12-unit apartment building in the middle of the complex.
“It was kinda chaos,” said Garcia.
RELATED: Residents urged to inspect chimneys after fire devastates Tower Point Condominiums
Garcia recorded video as he ran up to the burning apartment building. In the footage, flames can be seen on the roof. Fire officials say they believe the fire started in a chimney and then spread to the roof.
“The entire chimney itself was on fire,” said Joe Arrington with the San Antonio Fire Department.
When firefighters arrived, they immediately began evacuating people from the building. The apartment building was located in the center of the complex, just feet away from other buildings. One of those nearby residents was Kaitlyn Kennedy, whose apartment is right next door.
“The windows are gonna be really smoky, and there might be some warping to those too,” said Kennedy.
Eventually, the third floor of the building collapsed into the second floor. That’s when firefighters moved into a defensive position, spraying water from ladder trucks.
“There was a couple with their kids that just got out of the house,” said Garcia. “She was barefooted. I think the husband just got home.”
Fire officials say no one was hurt, and no other buildings caught fire.
“If the wind was going the other way, it probably would have been a lot different,” said neighbor Ellen Jensen.
Red Cross representatives say everyone who lost there home has a place to sleep. If you are affected by the fire and need help you can reach out to 800-733-2767.

content:
Fire breaks out in major London tower with black smoke seen
Several workers were forced to evacuate as a fire started in a major London tower, with a huge convoy of 60 firefighters flocking to the scene containing billowing black smoke
A huge fire has broken out in Canary Wharf, with black smoke seen billowing from a tower. A Morgan Stanley fire marshall told the Express the entire building has been evacuated.
Multiple fire engines can be seen parking outside, with part of the top floor of The Cabot in Canary Wharf currently on fire. The fire in on 25 Cabot Square, which is a 17-floor office building occupied by Morgan Stanley in Canary Wharf. One employee in the building told the Express: “It’s an electrical fire on the roof. We’ve all been told to leave”.
While it has not yet been confirmed what caused the fire, black smoke can be seen covering the skyline above the tower.
It is also understood that the road next to the building has been halted, with no traffic allowed to pass by the fire. The whole building has been evacuated, with workers lining up on the street, but it is not yet known how many floors have been affected.
A security officer has told the Express that it would be "a very long time" before workers would be allowed back into the building.
A statement from the London Fire Brigade says: "Eight fire engines and around 60 firefighters have been called to a fire in an electrical intake room on Cabot Square in Canary Wharf.
"An electrical intake room on the top floor of the building is currently alight.
"The Brigade was called at 1713 and is still on scene. The Brigade's 999 Control officers received 15 calls alerting them to the fire. They deployed crews from Poplar, Shadwell, Whitechapel, Plaistow, Dowgate, Euston, Dockhead, Shoreditch, Lewisham and East Greenwich fire stations.
"The cause of the fire is not known at this stage."
As well as the huge firefighter presence, an image from the scene shows numerous ambulances at the scene, with tape to cordon off an area next to the building in Canary Wharf.
Taking to X, London Fire Brigade wrote: "Eight fire engines and around 60 firefighters have been called to a fire in an electrical intake room on Cabot Square in #CanaryWharf. More info soon."
They later said the fire was due to an electrical issue. Writing on X, he said: "An electrical intake room on the top floor of a building in #CanaryWharf is currently alight. Our 999 Control officers have received 15 calls alerting them to the fire."

title: Portland apartment fire injures 3 , including firefighter in rescue
Firefighter injured , resident hospitalized in Portland apartment fire rescue
content:
Firefighter injured, resident hospitalized in Portland apartment fire rescue
PORTLAND, Ore. (KATU) — Portland Fire & Rescue crews faced a challenging Sunday morning as they responded to two separate fire incidents in the Northwest District.
The first call came just before 9 a.m. for a fire at a two-story apartment building located at 1233 NW 23rd and Overton.
Crews reported heavy fire and smoke from a second-story window once they arrived, with a person trapped inside.
Firefighters handled the blaze, while a separate fire truck conducted a vent/enter/isolate/search operation to rescue the trapped resident.
The person was then safely rescued through a window and transported in serious condition to Emanuel Hospital's Burn Center, suffering from smoke inhalation and burns.
Due to the urgency, fire crews transported the patient in their truck as the ambulance was still 10 minutes away.
During the rescue, a firefighter sustained a back injury and was taken to the hospital for evaluation.

The fire spread to a nearby apartment, leading to the hospitalization of another resident with minor injuries and smoke inhalation concerns.
Tragically, one dog and one cat died in the fire, though it remains unclear which apartment they belonged to.
The Red Cross and Animal Control were dispatched to assist three displaced residents and manage the removal of the deceased pets.
The fire was contained before reaching the attic or other apartments. The cause of the fire is under investigation, and authorities urge anyone with information to contact them.
Shortly after, a second incident was reported at a high-rise at 655 NW Hoyt St. Engine 4 arrived to find no visible fire, but audible alarms were sounding.
Crews discovered an unattended incense had ignited nearby paper items on the fifth floor. The small fire was quickly extinguished without activating the sprinkler system, and the incident was resolved.
Portland Fire & Rescue reminds residents of the dangers of unattended candles and incense, urging responsible use to prevent potential disasters. They also expressed gratitude to their partners, including BOEC, PPD, PGE, Red Cross, and Animal Control, for their assistance.

Residents fear deadly blaze in tower block with 'fire doors so bad a postman got trapped'
People living in a Brierley Hill tower say Dudley Council is fixing the wrong thing to stop fire doors staying open causing safety concerns
Residents of a Brierley Hill block of flats have spoken out about 'botched repairs' and perceived fire risks in their high rise block.
Diane Hobley said she had been raising concerns about the Dudley Council-owned Dean Court for 16 years but claimed she had not been taken seriously.
Mrs Hobley, aged 73, said fire doors on landings are blown open by wind coming through ventilation slats on the opposite wall and then do not close properly, creating a risk that fire could spread through the building.

Read more: Send parents demand action on special needs during poignant protest
Mrs Hobley said: "Gradually it got worse, the doors just wouldn't close. The council has tinkered with the doors, at one time they sent someone out every day to adjust the closer.
"They adjusted it and we couldn't open the door, the postman got stuck.
"We had to push the door open for him to get out and then the opposite happened where it was permanently open."
Gaynor English, aged 45, added: "They are trying to do things but they are not doing the right things, if we do it ourselves they will take it down.
"Even our front doors are no good, I can see daylight through mine."
Mrs Hobley said: "It's the slats, it's nothing to do with the doors, you could go to B&Q, get a block of wood and nail it to the thing, it would only cost £10."
With disasters like the Grenfell Tower fire of 2017 in their thoughts, residents said they would not be willing to wait in their homes during an emergency and trust the doors to keep flames at bay.
Mrs Hobley said: "It is in the back of your mind, especially if you smell an odd smell. I wouldn't wait an hour for a fire to be put out."
"It nearly did, nine years ago there was an old dear living opposite me – in the middle of the night I heard banging.
"It was the fire brigade, they were trying to break the door down.
"Smoke was coming out and one of the firemen came out with a pillow – she was smoking in bed so there was what could have been a fire."
A Dudley Council spokesperson told the Local Democracy Reporting Service the authority has emergency procedures to evacuate flats in the event of a fire.
The spokesperson added: "DMBC has a robust Fire Safety Management Plan aligned with the requirements of the Regulatory Reform (Fire Safety) Order 2005 this ensures DMBC's residential communal living sites are managed and maintained in such a way as to reduce the risks associated with fire and building safety.
"The council responds to all concerns raised in relation to building safety and compliance.
